SettingsOverridesType.doc: Declares configuration settings in a service manifest to be overridden. It consists of one or more sections of key-value pairs. Parameter values can be encrypted using the Invoke-ServiceFabricEncryptSecret cmdlet.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the section in the Settings.xml file to override.

children.name: Parameter
children.doc: The setting to override.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the setting to override.

attributes.name: Value
attributes.doc: The new value of the setting.

attributes.name: IsEncrypted
attributes.doc: If true, the value of this parameter is encrypted. The application developer is responsible for creating a certificate and using the Invoke-ServiceFabricEncryptSecret cmdlet to encrypt sensitive information. The certificate information that will be used to encrypt the value is specified in the Certificates section. This attribute is deprecated. Please use Type attribute.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: This value defines the type of value you have specified in the 'Value' Attribute. It can be SecretsStoreRef/Encrypted/PlainText. If set to SecretsStoreRef, we retrive the reference value from the SecretStore. If set to Encrypted, the application developer is responsible for creating a certificate and using the Invoke-ServiceFabricEncryptSecret cmdlet to encrypt sensitive information.

attributes.name: ApplicationTypeName
attributes.doc: The type identifier for this application.

attributes.name: ApplicationTypeVersion
attributes.doc: The version of this application type, an unstructured string.

attributes.name: ManifestId
attributes.doc: The identifier of this application manifest, an unstructured string.

children.name: Description
children.doc: Text describing this application.

children.name: Parameters
children.doc: Declares the parameters that are used in this application manifest. The value of these parameters can be supplied when the application is instantiated and can be used to override application or service configuration settings.

children.name: ServiceManifestImport
children.doc: Imports a service manifest created by the service developer. A service manifest must be imported for each constituent service in the application. Configuration overrides and policies can be declared for the service manifest.

children.name: ServiceTemplates
children.doc: Declares the set of permitted service types that can be created dynamically inside the application instance. Default configuration values, such as replication factor, are specified and used as a template for creating service instances.

children.name: Certificates
children.doc: Declares certificates used to secure endpoints or encrypt secrets within the application manifest or a cluster manifest.

ApplicationManifestType.doc: Declaratively describes the application type and version. One or more service manifests of the constituent services are referenced to compose an application type. Configuration settings of the constituent services can be overridden using parameterized application settings. Default services, service templates, principals, policies, diagnostics set-up, and certificates can also declared at the application level.

children.name: Parameter
children.doc: An application parameter to be used in this manifest. The parameter value can be changed during application instantiation, or, if no value is supplied the default value is used.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the parameter to be used in the manifest as "[Name]".

attributes.name: DefaultValue
attributes.doc: Default value for the parameter, used if the parameter value is not provided during application instantiation.

children.name: ConfigOverrides
children.doc: Describes configuration overrides for the imported service manifest. Configuration overrides allow the flexibility of re-using the same service manifests across multiple application types by overriding the service manifest's configuration only when used with a particular application type. Configuration overrides can change any default configuration in a service manifest as long as default configuration is defined using the Settings.xml in the ConfigPackage folder.

attributes.name: ServiceManifestName
attributes.doc: The name of the service manifest this is referenced. The name must match the Name declared in the ServiceManifest element of the service manifest.

attributes.name: ServiceManifestVersion
attributes.doc: The version of the service manifest that is referenced. The version must match the version declared in the service manifest.

ServiceManifestRefType.doc: Imports the service manifest by reference. Currently the service manifest file (ServiceManifest.xml) must be present in the build package.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the configuration package in the service manifest which contains the setting(s) to be overridden.

ConfigOverrideType.doc: Describes the configuration overrides for a particular config package in the imported service manifest.

children.name: Endpoints
children.doc: The service endpoint(s) to override.

ResourceOverridesType.doc: Specifies resource overrides for endpoints declared in service manifest resources.

children.name: Endpoint
children.doc: The endpoint, declared in the service manifest, to override.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the endpoint to override. A string.

attributes.name: Port
attributes.doc: The port number for the endpoint. Overrides the value in the service manifest.

attributes.name: Protocol
attributes.doc: The protocol for the endpoint. Overrides the value in the service manifest. HTTPS endpoints must also have an EndpointCertificate and an EndpointBindingPolicy declared in the application manifest. The protocol cannot be changed later in an application upgrade.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: The type of the endpoint. Overrides the value in the service manifest. Input endpoints are used to expose the port to the outside, internal endpoints are used for intra-application communication.

attributes.name: UriScheme
attributes.doc: The URI scheme. Overrides the value in the service manifest. For example, "http", "https", or "ftp".

attributes.name: PathSuffix
attributes.doc: The path suffix. For example, "/myapp1". Overrides the value in the service manifest.

children.name: EnvironmentVariable
children.doc: Environment variable.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: Name of environment variable.

children.name: EndpointBindingPolicy
children.doc: Specifies a certificate that should be returned to a client for an HTTPS endpoint.

children.name: ServiceFabricRuntimeAccessPolicy
children.doc: Specifies policies that determine how the service fabric runtime is exposed to the replicas.

children.name: ServicePackageResourceGovernancePolicy
children.doc: Defines the resource governance policy that is applied at the level of the entire service package.

children.name: ResourceGovernancePolicy
children.doc: Specifies resource limits for a codepackage.

children.name: ContainerHostPolicies
children.doc: Specifies policies for activating container hosts.

children.name: ConfigPackagePolicies
children.doc: Config Packages to be mounted inside the container.

children.name: NetworkPolicies
children.doc: Specifies network policies including container network policies.

children.name: IdentityBindingPolicy
children.doc: Binds a service defined identity to an application identity.

children.name: CodePackagePolicy
children.doc: Defines execution policies for CodePackages

ServiceManifestImportPoliciesType.doc: Describes policies (end-point binding, package sharing, run-as, and security access) to be applied on the imported service manifest.

attributes.name: CodePackageRef
attributes.doc: The name of the code package. Must match the name of the CodePackage specified in the service manifest.

attributes.name: UserRef
attributes.doc: The user account that the service code package will run as. The user account must be declared in the Principals section. Often it is preferable to run the setup entry point using a local system account rather than an administrators account.

attributes.name: EntryPointType
attributes.doc: Setup is the SetupEntryPoint declared in the service manifest, the privileged entry point that runs before any other entry point. Main is the EntryPoint declared in the service manifest, typically the long-running service host. All is all entry points.

RunAsPolicyType.doc: Specifies the local user or local system account that a service code package will run as. Domain accounts are supported on Windows Server deployments where Azure Active Directory is available. By default, applications run under the account that the Fabric.exe process runs under. Applications can also run as other accounts, which must be declared in the Principals section. If you apply a RunAs policy to a service, and the service manifest declares endpoint resources with the HTTP protocol, you must also specify a SecurityAccessPolicy to ensure that ports allocated to these endpoints are correctly access-control listed for the RunAs user account that the service runs under. For an HTTPS endpoint, you also have to define a EndpointBindingPolicy to indicate the name of the certificate to return to the client.

attributes.name: ResourceRef
attributes.doc: The resource being granted access to, declared and configured in the service manifest.

attributes.name: PrincipalRef
attributes.doc: The user or group being assigned access rights to a resource, must be declared in the Principals section.

attributes.name: GrantRights
attributes.doc: The rights to grant: Read, Change, or Full. The default is Read.

attributes.name: ResourceType
attributes.doc: The type of resource, defined in the Resources section of the service manifest. Either Endpoint or Certificate.

SecurityAccessPolicyType.doc: Grants access permissions to a principal on a resource (such as an endpoint) defined in a service manifest. Typically, it is very useful to control and restrict access of services to different resources in order to minimize security risks. This is especially important when the application is built from a collection of services from a marketplace which are developed by different developers.

attributes.name: PackageRef
attributes.doc: The name of the code, config, or data package to be shared. Must match the name of the package defined in the service manifest.

PackageSharingPolicyType.doc: Indicates if a code, config or data package should be shared across service instances of the same service type.

attributes.name: EndpointRef
attributes.doc: The name of the endpoint, which must be declared in the Resources section of the service manifest. When using HTTPS, do not use the same port and certificate for different service instances (independent of the application) deployed to the same node. Upgrading two different services using the same port in different application instances will result in an upgrade failure.

attributes.name: CertificateRef
attributes.doc: The name of the endpoint certificate, declared in the Certificates section, to return to the client.

attributes.name: RemoveServiceFabricRuntimeAccess
attributes.doc: Indicates if Fabric Runtime specific information should be exposed to the Code packages in the Service package.

attributes.name: CpuCores
attributes.doc: CPU request in number of logical cores for the service package. This value is considered when making placement decisions for the service package. Must have a value >=0.0001 when specified.

attributes.name: CpuCoresLimit
attributes.doc: CPU limit in number of logical cores for the service package. This value is considered when limiting CPU resources available to constituent code packages after placement of the service package on a node. Must have a value >=0.0001 when specified.

attributes.name: MemoryInMB
attributes.doc: Memory request in MB for the service package. This value is considered when making placement decisions for the service package. If both MemoryInMB and MemoryInMBLimit are not specified for a service package, then MemoryInMB for the service package is computed as the sum of MemoryInMB values of its constituent code packages. Must have a value >=4 when specified.

attributes.name: MemoryInMBLimit
attributes.doc: Reserved for future use.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: This is a user defined field. Ex: "GPU", "ExamplePlugin".

attributes.name: URI
attributes.doc: The connection string where to contact the specific plugin. Ex: '127.0.0.1:1234'.

attributes.name: PluginName
attributes.doc: This is a user defined field. It MUST match an entry in the 'ServicePackageResourceGovernancePolicy' 'ResourcePlugin' section.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: The type of resource these options describe. Must match one of the well known resource types. Ex: 'Device'.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: This is a user defined 'Name/Value' pair.

attributes.name: Value
attributes.doc: This is a user defined 'Value' associated to its 'Name'.

attributes.name: MemoryInMB
attributes.doc: Memory request in MB for the code package. MemoryInMB values of all the code packages in a service package are added to compute the total memory request for the service package if both MemoryInMB and MemoryInMBLimit are not specified for the service package. MemoryInMB is also used as the limit of memory allowed for the code package if MemoryInMBLimit is not specified. MemoryInMB must either be specified for all code packages in a service package or for none and must have a value >=4 when specified.

attributes.name: MemoryInMBLimit
attributes.doc: Memory limit in MB for the code package. Code packages are not allowed to allocate more memory than specified by this limit. MemoryInMBLimit values of all the code packages in a service package are added to compute the total memory limit for the service package if both MemoryInMB and MemoryInMBLimit are not specified for the service package. MemoryInMBLimit must either be specified for all code packages in a service package or for none and must have a value >=4 when specified.

attributes.name: MemorySwapInMB
attributes.doc: The total amount of swap memory that can be used, in MB. Must be a positive integer.

attributes.name: MemoryReservationInMB
attributes.doc: The soft limit (in MB) for memory governance that is enforced only when memory contention is detected on the node. Must be a positive integer.

attributes.name: CpuShares
attributes.doc: Relative CPU weight. Must be a positive integer. Cannot be used with CpuPercent, CpuCores, or CpuCoresLimit.

attributes.name: CpuPercent
attributes.doc: Usable percentage of available CPUs (Windows only). Must be a positive integer. Cannot be used with CpuShares, CpuCores, or CpuCoresLimit.

attributes.name: CpuCores
attributes.doc: Reserved for future use.

attributes.name: CpuCoresLimit
attributes.doc: Reserved for future use.

attributes.name: MaximumIOps
attributes.doc: Maximum IO rate (read and write) in terms of IOps that can be used. Must be a positive integer.

attributes.name: MaximumIOBandwidth
attributes.doc: The maximum IO (bytes per second) that can be used (read and write). Must be a positive integer.

attributes.name: BlockIOWeight
attributes.doc: Block IO weight, relative to other code packages. Must be a positive integer between 10 and 1000.

attributes.name: DiskQuotaInMB
attributes.doc: Disk quota for containers. Must be a positive integer.

attributes.name: KernelMemoryInMB
attributes.doc: Kernel memory limits in bytes. Must be a positive integer. Note this is Linux specific and docker on windows will error out if this is set.

attributes.name: ShmSizeInMB
attributes.doc: Size of /dev/shm in bytes. If omitted, the system uses 64MB. Must be a positive integer. Note this is Linux specific, however, docker will NOT error out if specified. It is simply ignored.

ResourceGovernancePolicyType.doc: Restricts the resources that can be used on the host and declares resource limits for a service code package.

attributes.name: Hostname
attributes.doc: Specify Hostname for container.

attributes.name: ContainerOS
attributes.doc: Specify operating system for container. Format must be "windows:NNNNN" where NNNNN is a windows build version, such as "windows:17763" or "windows:18362". Other values that are acceptable are "windows" and "linux". If value is unspecified, it defaults to 'windows'. Note that value is not used if isolation is not set to "hyperv". Also note that hyperv containers for windows is not supported below Windows OS Build 17763.

attributes.name: Isolation
attributes.doc: Isolation mode for container. Valid values are "default", "process" or "hyperv".

children.name: PortBinding
children.doc: Specifies which endpoint resource to bind container exposed port.

children.name: AdditionalOption
children.doc: Reserved for future use.

attributes.name: ContainerPort
attributes.doc: Container port number.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: Specify type of execution. Supported value is 'RunToCompletion'.

attributes.name: Restart
attributes.doc: Specify the restart policy applied on failure. Restart policy only refers to restart of code packages on the same node. Valid values are 'OnFailure' and "Never". Defaults to 'OnFailure' when not specified.

ExecutionPolicyType.doc: Specifies execution policy for service described in service manifest. Currently this is only supported for guest application.

attributes.name: UseDefaultRepositoryCredentials
attributes.doc: Use the default repository credentials specified in clusterManifest.xml instead of the credentials specified in the "RepositoryCredentials" tag inside ApplicationManifest.xml.

attributes.name: UseTokenAuthenticationCredentials
attributes.doc: Use MSI token authentication (or a custom specified endpoint) to obtain a token used for authentication.

attributes.name: Isolation
attributes.doc: Isolation mode for container. Valid values are default, process or hyperv (only supported for windows containers).

attributes.name: Hostname
attributes.doc: Specify Hostname for container.

attributes.name: ContainersRetentionCount
attributes.doc: Number of containers to leave behind when container repeatedly dies. By default this is set to 0 so no containers will be left behind.

attributes.name: AutoRemove
attributes.doc: Flag indicating whether removal of containers will occur automatically (true) or not (false) if the container is killed. If false SF manually remove the containers.

attributes.name: RunInteractive
attributes.doc: Run container with interactive flag enabled. Valid values are true/false. false by default.

attributes.name: Privileged
attributes.doc: Reserved for future use.

children.name: RepositoryCredentials
children.doc: Credentials for container image repository to pull images from. Use only one of RepositoryCredentials, RepositoryAuthentication.

children.name: RepositoryAuthentication
children.doc: Configuration for token-based authentication to containter image repository. Use only one of RepositoryCredentials, RepositoryAuthentication.

children.name: HealthConfig
children.doc: Specifies docker HEALTHCHECK integration options for the container.

children.name: PortBinding
children.doc: Specifies which endpoint resource to bind to the exposed container port.

children.name: CertificateRef
children.doc: Specifies information for a certificate which will be exposed to the container.

children.name: LogConfig
children.doc: Specifies the logging driver for a container.

children.name: NetworkConfig
children.doc: Specifies the network configuration for a container.

children.name: Volume
children.doc: Specifies the volume to be bound to container.

children.name: SecurityOption
children.doc: Specifies securityoptions for the container.

children.name: ImageOverrides
children.doc: Image names corresponding to OS build number to be launched.

children.name: Label
children.doc: Specifies the labels for the container.

children.name: AdditionalOption
children.doc: Reserved for future use.

attributes.name: AccountName
attributes.doc: User name or Service Account Name (for example, MyMachine\JohnDoe or John.Doe@department.contoso.com).

attributes.name: Password
attributes.doc: Password for the user account.

attributes.name: PasswordEncrypted
attributes.doc: Specifies if password is encrypted or plain text. This attribute is deprecated. Please use the 'Type' attribute to indicate encrypted password.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: This value defines the type of password you have specified in the 'Password' Attribute. It can be SecretsStoreRef/KeyVaultReference/Encrypted/PlainText. SecretsStoreRef: Value is of form {"key":"version"} 'key' is a azure resource and should be created before it can be used. KeyVaultReference: Value should be a valid versioned Keyvault secret identifier. Encrypted: Developer is responsible for creating a certificate and using the Invoke-ServiceFabricEncryptSecret cmdlet to encrypt sensitive information.

attributes.name: IdentityKind
attributes.doc: This value defines the type of identity to use to authenticate to ACR. Host: The identity of the compute under Service Fabric. In Azure, the VMSS Managed Identity. Service: The identity of the Service Fabric application. In Azure, the SF App Managed Identity. Cluster: The identity of the Service Fabric cluster.

attributes.name: IdentityRef
attributes.doc: This value defines the identifier of the identity to use to authenticate to ACR. SF App Managed Identity: The ServiceIdentityRef of the Service Fabric service VMSS Managed Identity: The client id of the User-Assigned Managed Identity. Can be left empty if using the System-Assigned identity, or the VMSS has only one identity.

attributes.name: IncludeDockerHealthStatusInSystemHealthReport
attributes.doc: If the container has HEALTHCHECK enabled and docker reports health_status event for this container, Service Fabric will include this as part of system reported health. When health_status is unhealthy Service Fabric will report a health warning. By default it is set to true.

attributes.name: RestartContainerOnUnhealthyDockerHealthStatus
attributes.doc: If the container has HEALTHCHECK enabled and docker reports health_status event for this container, Service Fabric will restart the container when health_status reported by docker is unhealthy. By default it is set to false.

attributes.name: TreatContainerUnhealthyStatusAsError
attributes.doc: If the container has HEALTHCHECK enabled and docker reports health_status event for this container, Service Fabric will report a health error when health_status is unhealthy. Service Fabric must be configured to include health_status as part of system reported health. By default it is set to false.

ContainerHealthConfigType.doc: Specifies docker HEALTHCHECK integration options for the container.

attributes.name: X509StoreName
attributes.doc: The store name for the X509 certificate.

attributes.name: X509FindValue
attributes.doc: The thumbprint of the X509 certificate.

attributes.name: DataPackageRef
attributes.doc: The name of data package that has the certificate files.

attributes.name: DataPackageVersion
attributes.doc: The version of data package that has the certificate files.

attributes.name: RelativePath
attributes.doc: The relative path to the certificate file inside data package.

attributes.name: Password
attributes.doc: Password/Private key for the certificate.

attributes.name: IsPasswordEncrypted
attributes.doc: If true, the value of password is encrypted.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: Identifier for the specific certificate information. This name is used to set the environment variable in the container.

ContainerCertificateType.doc: Specifies information about an X509 certificate which is to be exposed to the container environment. The certificate must be installed in the LocalMachine store of all the cluster nodes. When the application starts, the runtime reads the certificate and generates a PFX file and password (on Windows) or a PEM file (on Linux). The PFX file and password are accessible in the container using the Certificates_ServicePackageName_CodePackageName_CertName_PFX and Certificates_ServicePackageName_CodePackageName_CertName_Password environment variables. The PEM file is accessible in the container using the Certificates_ServicePackageName_CodePackageName_CertName_PEM and Certificates_ServicePackageName_CodePackageName_CertName_PrivateKey environment variables.

children.name: DriverOption
children.doc: Driver options to be passed to driver.

attributes.name: Name
attributes.doc: The name of the driver option.

attributes.name: Value
attributes.doc: The value of the driver option.

attributes.name: Type
attributes.doc: This value defines the protection of the value of the attribute. It may be SecretsStoreRef/Encrypted/PlainText. If set to SecretsStoreRef, the value references a secret stored encrypted in the cluster's SecureStore, which is de-referenced and decrypted upon activation. If set to Encrypted, the application developer is responsible for creating a certificate and using the Invoke-ServiceFabricEncryptSecret cmdlet to encrypt sensitive information.

DriverOptionType.doc: Driver options to be passed to driver. The Azure Files volume plugin supports the following driver options: shareName (the Azure Files file share that provides the volume for the container), storageAccountName (the Azure storage account that contains the Azure Files file share), storageAccountKey (Access key for the Azure storage account that contains the Azure Files file share). These three driver options are required.

attributes.name: NetworkType
attributes.doc: NetworkType. Currently supported types are "Open" and "Isolated".

attributes.name: Source
attributes.doc: The source folder which can be a folder in the VM that hosts the containers or a persistent remote store.

attributes.name: Destination
attributes.doc: The location that the Source is mapped to within the running container. Thus, your destination can't be a location that already exists within your container.

attributes.name: Driver
attributes.doc: The driver name for the Azure Files volume plugin is "sfazurefile".

children.name: DriverOption
children.doc: Driver options to be passed to driver.

children.name: Image
children.doc: Container image corresponding to OS build version number to be launched. If the Os attribute is not specified, the container image is assumed to work across all versions of the OS and overrides the image specified in the service manifest.

ImageOverridesType.doc: Windows Server containers may not be compatible across different versions of the OS. You can specify multiple OS images per container and tag them with the build versions of the OS. Get the build version of the OS by running "winver" at a Windows command prompt. If the underlying OS is build version 16299 (Windows Server version 1709), Service Fabric picks the container image tagged with Os="16299". An untagged container image is assumed to work across all versions of the OS and overrides the image specified in the service manifest.

attributes.name: Name
